page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a virtual instance configured with 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-assisted AES encryption. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with a 180 GB local NVMe SSD, and the platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate standard single-threaded compute metrics within median cloud ranges, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 1182.0 and a Clang compilation score of 5780.0. In-memory operations on cached data demonstrate consistent output, achieving 409.04 GB/s on small-block reads and 6.27 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks. However, multi-core throughput lands in lower distribution percentiles, as seen in a multi-core stress-ng rating of 5760.92, Geekbench multi-core score of 3820.0, and PassMark database operations at 1350.89.

The qualitative trade-off of this configuration pairs fast local NVMe storage with economical shared compute resources. Because physical cores are shared, the environment is subject to host contention during prolonged compute bursts. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance combined with local solid-state drives makes the instance suitable for lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, code compilation staging, and functional testing environments.
description: The Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is an entry-tier cloud instance within the High Performance lineup, featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 180 GB NVMe SSD. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES cryptography, backed by a 16 MB L3 cache. Benchmarks reflect moderate single-thread compute capabilities, achieving average tier results in Clang software compilation and Redis SET operations. However, heavy multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth fall within lower performance quartiles, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides cost-efficient entry-level capacity for tasks bounded by storage IO rather than sustained raw computation. The configuration is suitable for staging environments, continuous integration agents, lightweight web servers, and low-traffic caching layers.
